title: Prescription Insurance on File Pharmacy Billing Manual — Claim Submission Rules
content:
These clauses govern every claim Kestrel submits to a plan held under **Prescription Insurance on File**. Class settings named below are those of the plan class of the coverage record billed.

**B1. Active coverage only.** A claim is billed only to a coverage record in active status, as the coverage record shows it. A record pending verification, terminated or removed is not billed.

**B2. Days supply and timely filing.** A claim bills no more than the class's largest days supply per claim and is submitted no later than the date of service plus the class's timely filing days.

**B3. 90-day maintenance requirement.** Where the class carries the 90-day maintenance requirement, once the courtesy fills counted for a maintenance prescription in the current plan year reach the class's number of courtesy fills, the next claim must bill a 90-day supply, and a claim for 34 days or less is rejected plan limits exceeded. The courtesy fills counted are the paid claims for that prescription with a days supply of 34 or less, not reversed, dated in the current plan year.

**B4. Deductible.** Where the class has a pharmacy deductible phase, the patient pays the plan's full negotiated price until the deductible is met, except that a drug on the plan's preventive list is exempt where the class lets preventive-list drugs bypass the deductible.

**B5. Brand requested by the patient.** Where the class charges the brand-generic difference and the patient asked for the brand when a generic is available, the patient also pays the brand-generic difference. Where the class requires prior authorization for such a brand, the brand is rejected prior authorization required instead.

**B6. Per-claim cap and dispensing.** Where the class applies a per-claim patient-pay cap, the patient never pays more than the cap per claim: the patient pay after the cap is the lower of the patient pay the plan assigned and the cap. Where the class requires dispensing even if the copay is unpaid, a covered fill is dispensed even when the patient cannot pay.

**B7. Annual out-of-pocket cap.** Where the class applies an annual out-of-pocket cap and the patient pay on the coverage for the current plan year has reached that cap, patient pay is 0.00 for the rest of the plan year. The plan-year patient pay is the total of the patient pay on paid claims on the coverage dated in the plan year, less the patient pay of reversals on the coverage dated in the plan year.

**B8. Plan year.** The plan year runs by the class's plan-year setting: 1 January to 31 December for a calendar-year class, or from the anniversary of the coverage's effective date to the day before the next anniversary for an effective-date-anniversary class.

**B9. Specialty prescriptions.** A specialty prescription is billed through Kestrel only where Kestrel's specialty pharmacy is in the plan's specialty network; otherwise it is rejected specialty pharmacy required, and the patient may transfer it to the plan's specialty pharmacy.

**B10. Injury drugs.** Where the class bills only drugs for the accepted injury, only drugs for the accepted injury are billed.

**B11. Rejections.** Every rejection is resolved by the route the class names for its reject reason. A route the Patient Care Desk cannot carry out is explained to the patient, who may pay cash, or use a discount program where the class allows a discount program in lieu of the plan.

## Worked figures (hypothetical amounts)

| Clause | Facts | Result |
|---|---|---|
| B6 | Class cap of 8.00; plan assigns 12.40 | Patient pays 8.00 |
| B6 | Class cap of 8.00; plan assigns 5.00 | Patient pays 5.00 |
| B7 | Annual cap of 2100.00; plan-year paid-claim patient pay 2150.00, reversals 50.00 | Plan-year total 2100.00 has reached the cap; patient pay 0.00 for the rest of the plan year |
| B7 | Same cap; paid-claim patient pay 2150.00, reversals 80.00 | Plan-year total 2070.00 has not reached the cap |
| B3 | Class with 2 courtesy fills; two unreversed 30-day paid claims this plan year for a maintenance prescription | Next claim must bill 90 days; a 30-day claim is rejected plan limits exceeded |
